UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S OFFER OF RESOLUTION

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine offers to dismiss this entire action with prejudice against every Defendant on the following terms.

1.	The deposition. NCMEC will produce one witness under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 30(b)(6) for an examination not to exceed sixty minutes on the record. The examination is conducted by remote means and recorded stenographically and by video. Plaintiff pays the reporter and the videographer.

2.	The subjects. (a) NCMEC’s April 22, 2026 letters. (b) The two CyberTipline reports the letters identify, including whether NCMEC holds them, when it received each, and from whom. (c) The identifying information in each report as NCMEC originally received it, including whether either report contains the name “Marvelle J. Ballentine.” (d) The factual basis for the letters. No question will seek the content of any reported image or file or the identity of any person other than Plaintiff.

3.	What is not required. No payment. No admission of liability. No settlement conference. No particular answer. NCMEC may maintain every position it has taken in this action. Nothing is required of Hall or Meta.

4.	Performance. NCMEC performs when its designated witness answers, on the record and under oath, the questions put to the witness on the subjects in Paragraph 2. An appearance without answers is not performance. An invocation of any privilege against self-incrimination is not performance. A statement that the witness lacks knowledge of the two reports is not performance.

5.	Dismissal. Within seven days after Plaintiff receives the certified transcript of a performed examination, Plaintiff will file a notice dismissing this action with prejudice as to every Defendant under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i), each party to bear its own costs and fees. The obligation arises on performance. It does not arise on acceptance.

6.	Acceptance. NCMEC accepts by filing a notice of acceptance, signed by counsel of record, on the public docket of this action before expiration. That filing is NCMEC’s stipulation to the examination under Rules 26(d)(1), 29(a), and 30(a)(2)(A)(iii). The examination will be held within thirty days after acceptance. Plaintiff will give every party fourteen days’ notice of it. Silence is not acceptance. A counterproposal is not acceptance.

7.	Effective date and expiration. This Offer takes effect on service. It does not depend on any ruling on the Motion to which it is attached. It expires at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on December 9, 2026.

8.	Use. Plaintiff agrees to no restriction on the use of the transcript or the video record, subject to any court order or statute.

9.	Scope. This Offer concerns this action only. It releases no claim in any other action.

Date: November 16, 2026		                      Respectfully submitted,

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se

1520 Belle View Blvd, Ste. #5847

Alexandria, Virginia 22307

(407) 794-6503

jayballentine@protonmail.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

1.	Exhibit A, Plaintiff’s Offer of Resolution, with its Certificate of Service, Local Civil Rule 83.1(N) Certification, and Generative Artificial Intelligence Disclosure and Citation Certification.

Counsel of record for Defendants National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, Katie Hall, and Meta Platforms, Inc. are registered users of the Court’s Case Management/Electronic Case Filing (CM/ECF) system. Upon the Clerk’s docketing of the submission, the CM/ECF system will transmit a Notice of Electronic Filing to each of them, and service will be made through that means under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 5(b)(2)(E). EDSS submission is not itself service.

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se
